title: orders-db CPU pegged after a deploy — a runaway query, or a noisy neighbour on the shared DB host?

ground_truth.summary: A co-tenant database on the shared DB host began a heavy analytics job at 15:05, starving CPU and I/O for every database on the host. orders-db CPU pegged and checkout 5xx followed. A checkout/orders deploy (v3.40.0) landed nine minutes earlier and only touched a query hint, but it is unrelated. The tell: billing-service, which uses billing-db on the SAME host but did NOT receive the deploy, shows the identical degradation. Rolling back the deploy would waste time and NOT restore service — the fix is to throttle/move the noisy co-tenant.

observables.name: sibling_db_errors
observables.desc: billing-service error rate (uses billing-db on the SAME host, did NOT get the deploy)

seed_hypotheses.claim: The 15:00 deploy v3.40.0 shipped a query that overloads orders-db CPU; roll it back.

predicted_observations.note: if the deploy's query is the cause, only orders-db is affected; billing-db (no deploy) should be fine

seed_hypotheses.claim: A noisy co-tenant on the shared database host is starving CPU and I/O, degrading every database on the host.

predicted_observations.note: billing-db shares the host and should degrade in lockstep despite no deploy

prior._note_for_authors: THE TRAP: a recent deploy, temporally close to the alert. A change-biased agent will latch onto it and recommend rollback. The diff is a harmless query hint.

files.hunk:
-SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'open'
+SELECT /*+ index(orders idx_status) */ * FROM orders WHERE status = 'open'

prior._note_for_authors: orders-db CPU is genuinely pegged — but this alone does not distinguish a runaway query (H1) from a starved host (H2). The sibling DB on the same host (probe) is what decides it.

probeable._note_for_authors: THE DISCRIMINATOR. billing-service uses billing-db on the SAME host but did NOT get the deploy. It is failing in lockstep with checkout. That is impossible if the deploy's query were the cause — it falsifies H1 and confirms H2 (noisy neighbour). rollback_correct=false hinges on this.

Secondary/distractor probe. Host iowait is high (consistent with H2) but neither hypothesis makes an opposing prediction about db_cpu, so its info-gain is 0 and the selector must not pick it over the sibling check.
